ai.title: Strengthen endturn guidance to prevent premature turn ending
ai.summary: Updated backend system prompts in main-prompt.ts and agent-instructions.md to reinforce the requirement of completing all steps before emitting <end_turn>. Added explicit negative constraints and capitalized warnings to prevent the agent from ending turns prematurely during multi-step tasks. Scope limited to internal prompt engineering within the backend.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to do something, it now waits until every step is finished, including multi-part requests, before it signals it’s done. The behind-the-scenes instructions that guide how the assistant stops talking were strengthened so it can’t accidentally quit in the middle of a larger task. If you watched a session, you’d notice the assistant stays active and working through all the steps you gave it instead of pausing early.

ai.title: Add Vercel AI SDK support for finetuned Vertex models
ai.summary: Integrates `ai` and `@ai-sdk/google-vertex` to enable streaming and non-streaming prompts for finetuned Vertex AI models. New `vertexFinetuned` helper patches fetch requests to redirect standard Vertex endpoints to specific tuning job endpoints. Includes `ft_filepicker_003` in shared constants, cost tracking, and the `promptAiSdk` implementation.

eli5.text: The assistant software can now connect to and use a new kind of custom-trained AI model, allowing it to generate responses through either real-time streaming or complete delivery. Behind the scenes, it adds a new internal module that routes requests to a specific fine-tuned model endpoint, and it includes basic cost-tracking for usage of that model. A small example was left in the code showing how to try this new model, alongside notes indicating the team plans to clean up some temporary message conversion code. This is now in place and ready to use.

ai.title: Fix Context7 API integration
ai.summary: Context7 integration restored via new API endpoints. `context7ProjectsPromise` and `getContext7ProjectChunks` replaced by `context7LibrariesPromise` and `fetchContext7LibraryDocumentation`. Base URL updated to `https://context7.com/api`. `listContext7Projects` renamed to `listLibraries` with `SearchResponse` type. Timeout logic extracted to `timeoutPromise` helper.

eli5.text: The assistant can now pull in code documentation from a documentation service again, after an earlier connection method stopped working. Requests now go to the service's updated web address and use its newer lookup functions, so internal tool calls return documentation results instead of failing. This runs on the backend, so you as a user simply see documentation answers appearing again without any action on your part.

ai.title: Saxy emits raw text for schema-rejected tags
ai.summary: The Saxy streaming XML parser now emits raw tag text as a text node when a tag fails schema validation, replacing the previous silent ignore behavior. This change ensures that unknown or invalid tags are preserved in the output stream rather than dropped, improving data fidelity for downstream consumers. The update affects `common/src/util/saxy.ts`, specifically modifying `_handleTagOpening` and the main parsing loop to capture and emit `rawTag` strings for top-level and nested tag violations.

eli5.text: When the assistant's streaming XML parser encounters a tag that isn't allowed by the expected structure (like a <video> tag inside a list that only expects <item> tags), it now includes that tag's full text in the output instead of silently dropping it. This means you'll see the actual <video> text appear in your response stream rather than having it vanish completely. This affects any content that previously contained unexpected tags, which will now be visibly preserved instead of being stripped out.

ai.title: Saxy XML parser validates tag starts to fix rendering issues
ai.summary: Saxy parser now validates `<` characters against XML NameStartChar rules before treating them as tag starts. Previously, any `<` triggered tag parsing logic, causing rendering issues when literal `<` appeared in text nodes. The fix adds `_isXMLTagStart` helper and loops to find the next valid tag position. Affects `common/src/util/saxy.ts`.

eli5.text: If you write a literal less-than sign in your text, it no longer tricks the system into thinking it's the start of a special markup tag, which used to break how your content was displayed. Now the parser checks whether the character right after each less-than sign actually looks like the beginning of a real tag before trying to process one. You'll see your plain text render correctly even when it contains stray less-than characters. The fix is live today for anyone whose content flows through the core XML-style parser.

eli5.text: When the system connects to Google's AI service for special fine-tuned models, it had a small internal mismatch that confused the type-checking tools used during development. The fix corrects that mismatch so the connection setup reports no errors, with no effect on how the assistant actually works today. You wouldn't notice anything different; it's a behind-the-scenes correction for developers.

ai.title: Fix xml stream parser tests
ai.summary: Updated xml-stream-parser.test.ts to correct chunk splitting and expected output for text content processing. Removed verbose console.log statements from tool renderer callbacks. Adjusted test fixtures to include newlines within XML tags, aligning assertions with actual parser behavior.

eli5.text: Internal tests that check how streaming XML responses are broken into pieces were corrected so they match how the parser actually splits and reassembles text. Debug print statements were also removed from the tool-calling code, and the test sample data now contains line breaks inside XML tags to mirror real-world responses. You, as a reader, won't see any change in how the assistant behaves today, but these tests now guard against future regressions in how streamed text and tool calls are handled.

ai.title: Add usage-based credit billing with auto top-up
ai.summary: Freebuff now charges by the credit on Stripe invoices. The backend gains an auto top-up system in `common/src/billing/auto-topup.ts` that triggers `processAutoTopupPayment` and `checkAndTriggerAutoTopup` when a `UserProfile` balance falls below `auto_topup_threshold`, and `backend/src/websockets/middleware.ts` consumes credits through `consumeCredits` instead of the removed `quota-manager.ts`. The web app adds a 1 cent per credit pay-as-you-go model via `convertCreditsToUsdCents`, a new `/api/user/usage` endpoint, and a toggleable auto-topup UI in `web/src/components/auto-topup`.
ai.evidence: New file `common/src/billing/auto-topup.ts` exports `AutoTopupValidationError`, `AutoTopupPaymentError`, `validateAutoTopupStatus`, `disableAutoTopup`, `processAutoTopupPayment`, `checkAndTriggerAutoTopup`; `backend/src/index.ts` drops the `handler` export; `common/src/db/migrations/0014_wakeful_sinister_six.sql` creates `credit_ledger` and `grant_type` enum; `web/src/app/api/user/auto-topup/route.ts` exposes auto-topup settings endpoint.
ai.migration: If you previously relied on quota counters, you must migrate to the new credit balance API.
ai.unknowns: The drafts do not show when the new credit model rolls out to production users.

changes.what: Auto top-up logic with validation, payment processing, and threshold checks, plus credit conversion and grant priority ordering.
New credit ledger table, grant_type enum, and migration metadata for per-grant credit tracking.
WebSocket middleware consumes credits per message via consumeCredits, message cost tracking added, and auto topup endpoint wired into request flow.
Stripe webhooks create credit notes and revoke grants on refunds, pricing shifts to 1 cent per credit, and auto-topup toggle/settings UI added.
Unit tests cover auto topup threshold logic, credit conversion rounding, and usage calculation.

ai.summary: Expanded `request` type in `InsertMessageParams` to include `CoreMessage` in `backend/src/llm-apis/message-cost-tracker.ts`. This accommodates the new message format used by the cost tracker, preventing type errors when inserting records with `CoreMessage` arrays. The change is internal to the backend type definitions.

eli5.text: The system that tracks how much each conversation costs can now handle a newer kind of message format that the assistant uses when talking to some of the models behind the scenes. Nothing about what you see in the app changes, your chats look the same, but the cost-logging tool no longer trips over the new message type and silently drops or mis-records those conversations. It’s a behind-the-scenes fix inside the backend, already deployed, that keeps billing data accurate for the models that send messages in that format.

eli5.text: The Codebuff app has been re-released under a new version number, which bundles together the changes completed since the previous release. Updating installs today's improvements, which include a new interactive checkpoint menu and save command in the CLI, application of referral codes at login, referral instructions that now include a 'cd' command, support for OpenAI's o3 and o4-mini models in Freebuff, usage-based billing with automatic credit top-up, and support for finetuned Vertex AI models via the Vercel AI SDK. If you looked at your installed version, you would see it is now the latest one; the actual user-facing changes come from the features listed above rather than the label change itself.
